paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: knowing about Jesus is not the same as answering Him. The crowds had guesses, and they were nice ones. But then Jesus asks the disciples, "Who do you say I am?" (Matthew 16:15), and that question lands on every baker too. Peter's answer was, "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God." (Matthew 16:16) Jesus says that kind of answer comes from "My Father in heaven," not from "flesh and blood." (Matthew 16:17)

Now look at what happens next, because I LOVE this part. Peter gets the big answer right, and then he rebukes Jesus for saying He must suffer and be killed (Matthew 16:21-22). I can't laugh at Peter on this one, friend. I've been sure I knew better than the One who called me out of a junk drawer, and it never went well for me. Jesus tells Peter he has in mind "the things of men" instead of "the things of God." (Matthew 16:23) So the lesson is that the cross is God's way, even when our way looks a lot easier.

Then Jesus turns to all of His disciples and says anyone who wants to come after Him must "deny himself and take up his cross and follow Me." (Matthew 16:24) Holding tight to your own life loses it, and giving it up for His sake finds it (Matthew 16:25). Nothing in this whole world is worth trading your soul for (Matthew 16:26). And that's why my ovens stay ready, because the Son of Man will come in His Father's glory (Matthew 16:27). So, baker, who do YOU say He is, and are you following Him?
